title: Climate transition risk and corporate cash holdings evidence from China's agricultural sector
summary: Purpose This study aims to evaluate the impact of climate transition risk on agricultural firms' cash holdings, and to further explore the underlying mechanisms and economic consequence. Design/methodology/approach This study constructs a panel dataset from the annual reports of Chinese agricultural listed firms using textual analysis, and employs a fixed-effects model to explore the relationship between climate transition risk and cash holdings. Findings This study demonstrates that climate transition risk significantly reduces the cash holdings of agricultural firms. Corporate investment and financing constraints mediate this effect, while customer concentration moderates it. Firms located in western regions, large-scale firms, those with a high degree of digital transformation, and foreign-invested firms are better able to cushion the impact of climate transition risk on cash holdings. The influence of climate transition risk on cash holdings further leads to a reduction in operating profit margins. Originality/value This study makes a significant contribution to revealing the relationship between climate transition risk and cash holdings in agricultural firms.

title: Blockchain in supply chain finance: a systematic review and research agenda
summary: Purpose The paper aims to critically review the literature on applied blockchain, particularly in supply chain finance (SCF). It uses systematic literature review (SLR) to find, assess and synthesize peer-reviewed papers. The goal is to identify relevant areas of research and knowledge in existing literature, to highlight future research gaps and guide future studies. Design/methodology/approach It employs the PRISMA framework for systematic literature review to select papers for evaluation and synthesis. After applying the initial screening criteria, 583 records were identified. This was followed by qualitative filtering in which articles without citations and those from sources with a cite score less than one were excluded, resulting in 378 articles. After excluding the existing review studies, Title and abstract screening of remaining 351 articles was conducted to assess the amount of existing work on blockchain applications across various financial sectors, such as banking, insurance, SCF, entrepreneurial finance, cryptocurrency and more. It was found that there has been increasing research interest in the application of blockchain technology (BT) in SCF with 42 articles. In the next phase, structured narrative synthesis of these studies was conducted to examine use cases, research focus, methodologies and benefits. An analytical framework was developed and in the final phase, thematic foci and potential research questions were identified for future studies. The study also conducted methodological classification and comparative analysis to identify key findings and limitations. Findings The SLR findings identify the benefits, use cases and success factors for implementing BT and an analytical framework is developed to synthesis the existing literature covering application scenario-technological mechanism- implementation conditions-performance outcomes-research gaps. The main application scenario in SCF includes receivables financing, inventory and purchase order financing, and multi-tier credit facilitation, which are especially helpful for small and medium enterprises (SMEs), along with automation of back-end processes like KYC. Technological mechanisms through which the benefits are derived include distributed ledger, immutability, decentralised records, smart contracts, etc. The study emphasises that the factors influencing the implementation of technology in SCF include information transparency, management commitment, regulatory support, financial readiness, technological strength, etc. Performance outcomes of using blockchain in SCF include transparency, effectiveness, efficiency, credibility, trust, reliability and resilience. Originality/value Blockchain technology has been widely adopted across various industries. Despite a recent rise, scholarly interest in this field remains limited, as the technology landscape is dynamic and developments happen rapidly. This study critically reviews the literature on applied blockchain, specifically in SCF, contributing a novel perspective to existing research.

title: Challenges and Prospects of Digital Technology Utilization among Library Personnel in Adamawa State University, Mubi
summary: This study investigates the challenges and prospects of digital technology utilization among library personnel at Adamawa State University, Mubi. A descriptive survey design was adopted, with a population of 46 library staff. Data collected through structured questionnaires were analyzed using SPSS version 25. Findings revealed that major challenges affecting digital technology use include frequent power outages (mean = 4.44), poor internet connectivity (mean = 4.30), inadequate ICT training (mean = 4.28), and insufficient funding (mean = 4.16). Despite these challenges, utilization levels were moderate to high, particularly in the use of OPAC and automation software. Prospects for improving digital utilization were strongly identified, such as regular digital literacy training, improved ICT infrastructure, and increased funding. Inferential analysis indicated significant relationships between technology availability, staff competence, and utilization (p < 0.05). The study concludes that addressing infrastructural and skill gaps through continuous training and improved digital support systems will enhance service efficiency and promote sustainable digital transformation in academic libraries.

title: Shared Signing Auditors and Corporate ESG Performance: Hand in Hand or Out of Step?
summary: ABSTRACT As environmental, social, and governance (ESG) considerations become increasingly pivotal to investment decisions, regulatory agendas, and corporate strategies, the diffusion of sustainable practices across firms has emerged as a critical concern. Auditors who serve multiple clients may act as conduits for the cross‐firm transmission of ESG knowledge and norms. Drawing on social network theory and organizational learning theory, this study examines whether sharing signing auditors with high‐ESG peers enhances corporate ESG performance. Using a comprehensive sample of Chinese A‐share listed firms from 2009 to 2025, we document that firms sharing signing auditors with high‐ESG peers exhibit significantly better ESG outcomes, consistent with a “hand‐in‐hand” convergence effect rather than an “out‐of‐step” divergence. This finding remains robust to a series of endogeneity and robustness tests. Moderation analyses show that the positive effect is amplified when executives have environmental backgrounds but attenuated by greater institutional investor attention, underscoring the roles of managerial receptivity and external governance substitution in shaping the diffusion process. Further analyses reveal that the ESG improvements resulting from shared signing auditors translate into enhanced stock returns and stronger sustainable development capacity. This study advances research on ESG determinants and auditor networks by identifying shared signing auditors as interorganizational knowledge brokers that facilitate the diffusion of sustainability‐related knowledge and practices, offering practical implications for firms, audit professionals, and regulators.

title: Microeconomic Foundations of Corporate Governance and Small and Medium Enterprises Performance: Evidence from Central Asia
summary: This article explores the microeconomic foundations connecting corporate governance mechanisms to the operational performance of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Central Asia. Most corporate governance research focuses heavily on large public corporations. As a result, small enterprises in transition economies are often misunderstood-they are forced to adopt rigid, big-company compliance rules rather than practical, scaled-down tools that solve their real-world contracting problems. Using reliable data from the World Bank Enterprise Surveys, this study examines how both internal firm governance and external regional challenges shape SME growth across Central Asia. The findings reveal that internal governance quality, specifically financial disclosure proxying by external audits, exerts a positive and statistically significant impact on SME performance. By integrating microeconomic theories of corporate governance with evidence on the regional business environment, this study aims to contribute a context-sensitive analytical framework for examining SME performance in emerging economies. The proposed framework may also inform policy discussions on strengthening business institutions, improving access to finance, and supporting sustainable SME development in Central Asia.

title: Sustainable supply chain network design with pooling
summary: Faced with numerous operational and sustainability challenges, logistics systems require innovative solutions. Pooling logistics offers a practical solution by allowing resources to be shared and system performance to be improved. To better understand its potential, this study investigates a sustainable two-echelon supply chain network design (STESCND) model by comparing pooling and non-pooling scenarios under heterogeneous vehicle fleets. An optimization model based on mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) is developed, incorporating sustainability dimensions. To capture the full scope of sustainability, the model considers economic, environmental, and social dimensions, focusing respectively on cost minimization, reduction of CO2 emissions, and minimization of accident rates. The solution methodology is carried out in two stages. First, a mono-objective optimization is performed for each sustainability dimension separately. The results indicate that pooling can reduce total costs by 44% and 2 emissions by 49%, while affecting the accident rate by 11%. Second, a multi-objective optimization approach is applied using the ε-constraint method to analyze the trade-offs among the three dimensions. The multi-objective results show that this approach provides better-balanced solutions, providing valuable insights into the benefits of resource pooling and the inherent compromises between sustainability objectives.

title: Effect of Financial Technology Adoption on the Financial Performance of Deposit-Taking Savings and Credit Cooperative Societies (SACCOs) in Kenya
summary: Purpose: The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of financial technology adoption on the financial performance of deposit-taking savings and credit cooperative societies (SACCOs) in Kenya. Methodology: The study adopted a desktop research methodology. Desk research refers to secondary data or that which can be collected without fieldwork. Desk research is basically involved in collecting data from existing resources hence it is often considered a low-cost technique as compared to field research, as the main cost is involved in executive’s time, telephone charges and directories. Thus, the study relied on already published studies, reports and statistics. This secondary data was easily accessed through the online journals and library. Findings: The study suggests that financial technology adoption, particularly mobile banking, digital lending, internet banking and automated financial management systems, has the potential to positively influence the financial performance of deposit-taking SACCOs in Kenya. Adoption of these technologies may enhance operational efficiency, reduce transaction costs, improve loan management and increase profitability. However, the extent of these benefits depends on effective technology implementation, institutional capacity, cybersecurity measures and members’ utilization of digital financial services. Unique Contribution to Theory, Practice and Policy: The technology organization environment framework, diffusion of innovations theory & financial intermediation theory may be used to anchor future studies on effect of financial technology adoption on the financial performance of deposit-taking savings and credit cooperative societies (SACCOs) in Kenya. The study is expected to provide practical insights that will assist SACCO managers, boards of directors and financial technology providers in making evidence-based decisions regarding digital transformation investments. The study is expected to provide empirical evidence to inform the development and improvement of policies governing financial technology adoption among deposit-taking SACCOs in Kenya.

title: Integrating ISSM and TTF to Evaluate Mandatory System Success: A Pathway to Paperless Sustainability
summary: Background: Digital transformation toward paperless bureaucracy has become a strategic necessity for organizations seeking to reduce administrative risk and environmental impact, yet mandatory information systems are frequently evaluated using models that assume voluntary adoption. Objective: This study appraises the implementation success of a mandatory online Travel Management System (Surat Perjalanan Dinas/SPD) by combining the Information Systems Success Model (ISSM) with Task-Technology Fit (TTF), applying Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to 109 users at PT XYZ. Methods: Every measurement item satisfied the requisite convergent validity, discriminant validity, and reliability thresholds before structural model testing. The findings establish that System Quality, Information Quality, and Service Quality jointly influence User Satisfaction, whereas Task Characteristics and Technology Characteristics strongly determine Task-Technology Fit (TTF). Results: As a primary finding, User Satisfaction does not significantly affect TTF, confirming that in a mandatory use environment, task-fit evaluation is based purely on objective feature capability rather than users' affective emotional bias. Ultimately, the achievement of Net Benefits is strongly predicted by TTF, confirming that bureaucratic efficiency can only be realized when technological functionality perfectly accommodates operational field demands. Conclusion: These findings extend ISSM-TTF theory to compulsory-use contexts and offer practical guidance for organizations pursuing paperless sustainability.

title: Digital accounting implementation and perceived operational performance in Vietnamese commercial banks: Empirical evidence from accountants and managers
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThis study examines the relationships among digital accounting implementation, financial reporting quality, usefulness of accounting information, top management support, and perceived operational performance in commercial banks. Data were collected from 562 accountants and managers working at 27 commercial banks in Vietnam, an emerging Asian economy. The study evaluated the proposed model using a two-stage Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling approach. The findings indicate that digital accounting implementation is positively associated with perceived operational performance. In addition, digital accounting implementation is indirectly associated with perceived operational performance through statistically significant indirect paths involving financial reporting quality and usefulness of accounting information. Financial reporting quality is also positively associated with the usefulness of accounting information. Furthermore, the positive associations between digital accounting implementation and both financial reporting quality and usefulness of accounting information were stronger at higher levels of perceived top management support, whereas the interaction between digital accounting implementation and perceived operational performance was not statistically significant. Collectively, the findings suggest that perceptions of digital accounting implementation are closely related to perceptions of information quality, information usefulness, managerial support, and perceived operational performance. This study contributes empirical evidence on the interrelationships among these perceived organizational constructs in the context of banking digital transformation in an emerging economy.

title: Improving Financial Literacy: From Corporate Finance to Personal Finance
summary: This article provides an overview of the literature on financial literacy. It covers the initial measurement that created the Big Three financial literacy questions and measures of personal finance knowledge featuring 28 questions. It shows that levels of financial literacy are low and have not been improving over time. This is true not only in the United States but also in countries worldwide. These findings matter because financial literacy is conducive to savvy financial behaviors, from holding precautionary savings to planning for retirement to many other financial decisions. Financial education programs have grown exponentially over time, providing important insights into their cost-effectiveness. Personal finance courses have been added to high school and college curricula, and the evidence indicates that they are useful initiatives to improve financial knowledge and downstream behavior.

title: Capital Market Development and Economic Transformation in Nigeria
summary: The study determined the nature of the relationship capital market development and economic growth in Nigeria during 1990 – 2024. The data for the period under consideration were sourced from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) Statistical Bulletin for annual time-series analysis; the economic growth indicator used was real GDP growth while total market capitalization was used as the measure of the capital market development. Control variables included money supply, private sector credit and inflation. The Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) method was used to analyse the short and long run relationships between the variables. A long run relationship was confirmed with the bounds test. In the long run, the impact of market capitalization and money supply are positive for economic growth while the impact of private sector credit and inflation are negative. In the short run, the capitalization of a market has positive and significant impact on both the contemporaneous and lagged changes in the economic growth, while the money supply has negative and significant impact on the economic growth. Inflation has a negative contemporaneous effect but positive and significant effects at its first and second lags; private sector credit has no significant short-run effect. The disequilibration correction coefficient is negative and significant, which means there is a high rate of correction of about 91.8% or more of the disequilibrium in one year. The study found that capital market development has relevance to Nigeria’s economic development but its impact is moderated by the general state of the monetary and macro economic conditions. It suggests policies to increase market depth, build investor confidence, increase long-term capital inflows and to optimize monetary and credit management to boost the contribution of the capital market to economic growth.

title: "Digital Transformation in Indian Banking: A Case study of Indian Bank"
summary: This case study examines the digital transformation journey of Indian Bank, highlighting how a century-old public sector institution transitioned from conventional branch-centric operations to technology-driven banking. The report explores critical modernization milestones, including the implementation of 100% Core Banking Solutions (CBS) and strategic flagships like Project WAVE (World of Advanced Virtual Experience) and the IndSMART mobile platform. It provides an analytical overview of process shifts across account opening, paperless lending, digital payments (UPI, NEFT, IMPS), and customer support. Drawing on key metrics from FY 2024–25—such as a ₹1.67 lakh crore digital business volume, 95% digital savings account openings, and 92% digital transaction share—the document evaluates the tangible advantages in operational efficiency alongside structural challenges involving cybersecurity, infrastructure costs, technical uptime, and rural digital literacy.

title: Identifying contemporary challenges in the banking sector: a fuzzy Delphi study of Bank Melli Iran
summary: Purpose This study aims to develop an expert-supported framework of contemporary banking challenges using a sequential mixed-methods design and a fuzzy Delphi study involving senior managers from Bank Melli Iran. Design/methodology/approach This research began with a systematic review of 15 studies to create an initial framework for current banking challenges. The framework was improved after three interviews with senior banking executives. Next, a fuzzy Delphi study was used to evaluate the updated indicators, drawing on a panel of 30 senior managers and experts from Bank Melli, Iran. All questionnaires were distributed and collected by the end of 2025. Findings The analysis identified five key dimensions of contemporary banking challenges and retained 46 of the 48 proposed indicators after the fuzzy Delphi evaluation. Anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing, cybersecurity with consumer data privacy protection, weak internet infrastructure, generational gaps in technology adoption and lack of integration across banking systems were among the indicators receiving the strongest expert support. The results indicated a high level of expert consensus (overall Kendall’s W = 0.890, p < 0.001), and threshold sensitivity and robustness analyses confirmed the stability of the proposed framework. Originality/value This research advances contemporary banking literature by transcending fragmented analyses of digital transformation, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, regulation and financial technology to establish an integrated, expert-driven indicator framework. Instead of introducing a universal taxonomy, this study presents a contextually grounded managerial assessment framework tailored to large legacy banks in developing economies, thereby establishing a robust basis for future cross-institutional and cross-country validation.

title: DYNAMIC BEHAVIOURAL SEGMENTATION IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY
summary: Digital technologies have changed how firms observe and classify consumers. Traditional segmentation based on static demographic, geographic and psychographic variables is increasingly unable to capture behaviour that changes from day to day on digital platforms. This paper examines dynamic behavioural segmentation, an approach in which customers are grouped and regrouped continuously on the basis of real-time digital footprints and adaptive analytics. Using a conceptual review of the literature on marketing analytics, customer experience and data mining, the paper compares traditional and dynamic approaches, proposes a six-stage conceptual model, and identifies the behavioural indicators on which dynamic segmentation relies. The analysis suggests that the approach improves targeting, supports early retention measures and shortens the response time between behavioural change and marketing action, while raising issues of privacy, transparency and data governance. The paper concludes that dynamic behavioural segmentation represents a paradigm shift in customer analytics in the digital economy.

title: FinTech, transparency, governance and financial inclusion: channels to sustainable development goals in Gulf Cooperation Council banking
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine how banking digitalization and FinTech development advance the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) banks, focusing on transparency, governance and financial inclusion as the channels linking FinTech to sustainability. Design/methodology/approach To explore the relationship between digitalization and SDGs in GCC banks, the authors construct a FinTech Engagement Index (FEI) and a Sustainability Engagement Index (SEI) for 69 GCC banks over 2020–2023. A GLS regression model estimates this relationship, controlling for bank-specific characteristics and macroeconomic conditions. Findings The results of this study reveal a significant positive relationship between FinTech adoption and banking sector sustainability, demonstrating that advanced digitalization enhances transparency, governance and financial inclusion while accelerating progress toward SDGs. Institutional characteristics play a meaningful role in this relationship. These results are valuable for policymakers and regulators aiming to leverage FinTech for sustainable banking development. Practical implications Policymakers should foster FinTech innovation while ensuring risk management and consumer protection. Bank leaders should use FinTech as a strategic sustainability tool, prioritizing digital platforms for green products, automated reporting and environmental monitoring. Legacy banks should embed sustainability into digital transformation from the outset, while GCC regulators can promote adoption through incentives such as favorable reserve requirements or expedited licensing for FinTech-linked sustainable finance products. Social implications Sustainable, FinTech-enabled banking advances social equity by expanding financial inclusion. Policymakers should require banks to integrate social metrics, such as microfinance, women-owned business support and community reinvestment, into sustainability frameworks and help Islamic banks translate ethical principles into measurable outcomes. Originality/value This paper constructs novel bank-level indices to quantify digitalization and sustainability in GCC banking, provides among the first evidence explicitly linking FinTech engagement to specific SDGs in the region and translates the findings into a regulatory framework for named GCC policymakers.

title: Financing Healthcare Sustainability Through Responsible Banking: A Policy Framework for Bangladesh
summary: Bangladesh's health system faces a dual sustainability crisis. On the financing side, public health expenditure has remained below one per cent of GDP for two decades, while out-of-pocket payments account for roughly two-thirds of total health spending — among the highest ratios in South Asia — pushing households into poverty and stalling progress toward Universal Health Coverage. On the environmental side, healthcare is a globally carbon-intensive sector whose facilities, energy use and supply chains contribute materially to emissions even as the sector's mission is to protect health. This paper argues that responsible banking — the alignment of lending and investment with sustainability objectives under frameworks such as the UN Principles for Responsible Banking, and, domestically, Bangladesh Bank's Sustainable Finance Policy — offers an underused channel for addressing both dimensions simultaneously. Using a review of national budget documents, central-bank circulars, capital-market records and international benchmarks from 2016 to 2025, the paper maps the instruments through which responsible finance can mobilise capital for resilient, low-carbon and financially inclusive healthcare: green and social bonds, sustainability-linked loans, concessional green refinancing, blended finance and health micro-insurance. It finds that Bangladesh has built credible sustainable-finance rails — including four concessional refinancing funds and a pioneering green-bond framework — but has yet to direct them deliberately at the health sector. The paper concludes with a set of policy recommendations to bridge the health-financing gap through responsible banking while safeguarding against greenwashing and inequitable access. title: Green Finance and Sustainable Investment Strategies for Climate-Resilient Economies
summary: Climate shocks are making economic fragility more costly, and green finance is becoming more important for financing investments that mitigate it. This paper explores the relationship between green finance intensity and the nature of sustainable investment strategies with respect to climate resilience, covering 96 economies categorized into four groups (advanced, emerging Asian, other emerging, and low-income economies). Six of these instruments were merged with a green finance intensity index, a climate resilience index, and carbon-intensity reduction to create the portfolio shares across the instruments. The sharply different financing models revealed in the results are evident: green bonds occupy 30.7 percent of portfolios in the advanced economies, but only 6.2 percent in the low-income economies, while resilient and adaptation infrastructure have the highest share in the latter (29.9 percent). There is a strong association between Green Finance intensity and Resilience (r = 0.86), with decreasing marginal returns beyond higher levels of intensity; while controlling for income and intensity, there is still explanatory power for adaptation spending (R² = 0.81). The results validate a differentiated approach: scale and diversify capital investments in places where there is low intensity, and focus investments in places where resilience needs are highest, in terms of adaptation.

title: DIGITAL ENTREPRENEURIAL TRANSFORMATION IN THE PESANTREN ECOSYSTEM: EVIDENCE FROM PESANTREN AL AMIN KEDIRI, INDONESIA
summary: ABSTRACT Pesantren, as traditional Islamic educational institutions, increasingly adopt digital technologies to strengthen economic self-reliance through entrepreneurship. This study aimed to analyze digital marketing strategies implemented by santri at Pesantren Al Amin Kediri and their contributions to business development. This research employed a descriptive qualitative case study approach. Data were collected through participatory observation, in-depth interviews, documentation, and digital content analysis of Instagram, WhatsApp Business, and TikTok. The analysis integrated the Digital Marketing Framework and Resource-Based View (RBV) to examine digital capabilities and internal resources as sources of competitive advantage. The findings indicate that santri contribute to digital transformation through content creation, social media engagement, digital branding, and online customer communication. These practices have expanded the market reach of Al Amin Bordir dan Konveksi, enhanced brand visibility, and strengthened customer relationships. Spiritual values, entrepreneurial learning, and alumni networks further reinforce customer trust and business sustainability. The study contributes theoretically by extending the application of RBV to pesantren-based digital entrepreneurship, demonstrating how spiritual values, social capital, and trust-based relationships complement technological capabilities in creating competitive advantage. Practically, the study contributes an integrated approach to digital entrepreneurship that emphasizes santri empowerment, digital marketing skills, and alumni engagement while preserving religious and cultural identities. This study concludes that digital marketing functions not merely as a promotional instrument but also as a mechanism for entrepreneurial learning, economic empowerment, and sustainable business development within faith-based educational institutions. Keywords: digital marketing; faith-based entrepreneurship; pesantren entrepreneurship; resource-based view; santri empowerment ABSTRAK Pesantren sebagai lembaga pendidikan Islam tradisional semakin mengadopsi teknologi digital untuk memperkuat kemandirian ekonomi melalui kegiatan kewirausahaan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis strategi pemasaran digital yang diterapkan oleh santri di Pesantren Al Amin Kediri serta kontribusinya terhadap pengembangan usaha. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan metode studi kasus. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi partisipatif, wawancara mendalam, dokumentasi, serta analisis konten digital pada Instagram, WhatsApp Business, dan TikTok. Analisis dilakukan menggunakan Digital Marketing Framework dan Resource-Based View (RBV) untuk mengidentifikasi kapabilitas digital dan sumber daya internal sebagai sumber keunggulan kompetitif. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa santri berperan aktif dalam transformasi digital melalui pembuatan konten, pengelolaan media sosial, penguatan merek digital, dan komunikasi pelanggan secara daring. Strategi tersebut mampu memperluas jangkauan pasar Al Amin Bordir dan Konveksi, meningkatkan visibilitas merek, serta memperkuat hubungan dengan pelanggan. Nilai-nilai spiritual, pembelajaran kewirausahaan, dan jaringan alumni turut memperkuat kepercayaan pelanggan serta keberlanjutan usaha. Kontribusi teoretis penelitian ini adalah memperluas penerapan RBV dalam kewirausahaan digital berbasis pesantren dengan menunjukkan bahwa nilai spiritual, modal sosial, dan hubungan berbasis kepercayaan melengkapi kapabilitas teknologi dalam menciptakan keunggulan kompetitif. Secara praktis, penelitian ini berkontribusi dalam menawarkan pendekatan kewirausahaan digital terintegrasi yang menekankan pemberdayaan santri, penguatan keterampilan pemasaran digital, dan pemanfaatan jaringan alumni tanpa mengabaikan identitas keagamaan dan budaya. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa pemasaran digital tidak hanya berfungsi sebagai sarana promosi, tetapi juga sebagai instrumen pembelajaran kewirausahaan, pemberdayaan ekonomi, dan pengembangan usaha berkelanjutan dalam ekosistem pendidikan berbasis keagamaan. title: ESG Engagement in Operations Management: A Systematic Literature Review and Research Agenda
summary: ABSTRACT Operations management (OM) research remains fragmented in explaining how firms translate environmental, social, and governance (ESG)‐related pressures and commitments into operational practices through stakeholder engagement. To address this gap, this study systematically reviews 136 peer‐reviewed articles published between 2004 and 2024 and develops an integrative process‐oriented framework organized around three main domains: contextual drivers, salient stakeholders, and operational enactment activities. The synthesis identifies three key challenges in the translation process—prioritization, participation, and execution—and develops corresponding research directions centered on adaptive benchmarking, connectivity and integration, and materiality grounding. The framework clarifies how firms interpret contextual pressures with stakeholders and embed ESG commitments in organizational decisions and activities. The study thereby advances a more coherent understanding of how OM can connect strategic ESG commitments with substantive operational practices.

title: Land use efficiency in the era of digital transformations: experience of China’s land resource management
summary: The article presents a comprehensive institutional, spatial, and econometric analysis of land resource management transformation driven by digitalization, focusing on the experience of the People’s Republic of China, and outlines conceptual directions for adapting these practices to Ukraine’s post-war recovery. The study substantiates Green Land Use Efficiency (GLUE) as an advanced paradigm that integrates economic productivity with environmental risk minimization, resource saving, and carbon footprint reduction in the context of sustainable spatial development. The research thoroughly investigates China’s pivotal 2018 institutional reform, which eliminated interagency fragmentation by establishing the Ministry of Natural Resources and implementing the “multi-plan integration” (Duogui Heyi) framework. The engineering and technological foundations of the National Territorial Spatial Planning “One Map” platform are revealed alongside the “Tiandi Wang” dynamic monitoring system (RS + AI + Beidou) and the “three zones and three lines” spatial control framework. The paper systematizes the mathematical apparatus for measuring GLUE based on non-radial Super-SBM models (accounting for undesirable outputs) and Spatial Durbin Models (SDM), and empirically verifies initial spatial siphoning and subsequent green spillover effects across neighboring regions. Furthermore, the paper highlights sectoral and spatial specificities of land digitalization: the deployment of 3D/4D cadastral modeling, BIM, and Digital Twin Cities in densely populated urban agglomerations, versus electronic farmland circulation platforms (Sanquan Fengli) and satellite-driven precision agriculture in rural regions. The analysis also identifies key structural risks, including regional digital divides, local fiscal dependencies on land finance, and data security vulnerabilities. Finally, the study proposes practical directions for modernizing Ukraine’s spatial management. These include creating a unified National GIS Superplatform compliant with EU INSPIRE standards, deploying AI-driven satellite monitoring for war-damage auditing and mine-clearance prioritization, and legally establishing a digital spatial framework for recovery and ecological-protection lines. Keywords: Green Land Use Efficiency (GLUE), digital transformation, GIS platforms, One Map system, “three zones and three lines”, Super-SBM model, Spatial Durbin Model, post-war recovery of Ukraine, Beidou, State Land Cadastre.

title: Prioritizing sustainable supply chain capability for bio-circular-green economy implementation in agri-food supply chains: A circular intuitionistic fuzzy approach
summary: Agri-food supply chains play a critical role in sustainable development but continue to face challenges related to resource-intensive production, food loss, and environmental impacts. The Bio-Circular-Green (BCG) economy offers an integrated pathway toward sustainability through bio-based resource utilization, circular material flows, and environmentally responsible operations. This study proposes an integrated Circular Intuitionistic Fuzzy Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (CIF-MCDM) framework with Quality Function Deployment (QFD) to prioritize sustainable supply-chain capabilities (SSCCs) supporting BCG implementation in agri-food systems. Grounded in the Resource-Based View (RBV) and Dynamic Capabilities View (DCV), the framework incorporates stakeholder priorities, capability interdependencies, and uncertainty in expert judgments within a unified decision-support structure. An end-to-end rice supply chain under Thailand's Royal Patronage BCG pilot project is employed as the case study. The methodological contribution lies in integrating CIF theory with deployment-oriented capability analysis to simultaneously evaluate stakeholder requirements, causal interrelationships, and strategic capability priorities under uncertainty. The results identify bio-quality and food safety compliance, traceability, and waste reduction as the most critical stakeholder requirements for BCG implementation. After incorporating network interdependencies, the top three prioritized SSCCs are closed-loop coordination and stakeholder engagement, circular reuse, recycling, and responsible disposal, and reverse logistics and recovery management. The findings demonstrate that circular and return-oriented capabilities exert the strongest systemic influence on BCG supply-chain performance. From a managerial perspective, organizations should prioritize integrated circular coordination mechanisms and reverse logistics infrastructures before pursuing advanced sustainability initiatives to strengthen long-term sustainability, resilience, and circularity performance.

title: Market-Average Data Can Misrepresent Supply Chain Environmental Impacts and Their Uncertainty
summary: Abstract Market-average data sets are often used in life cycle assessment and carbon accounting when the production route of a procured good is unknown. The uncertainty this introduces is commonly characterized using generic pedigree matrix factors, which do not reflect how variability across production geographies and technologies differs between goods. Here, we develop a hybrid method that combines pedigree matrix uncertainty characterization within individual production routes with market-share-weighted Monte Carlo sampling between known production routes to represent uncertainty about which route supplied the good. We compare it with conventional market-average uncertainty analysis for 30 economically important goods. For climate impacts, conventional 5th–95th interpercentile intervals are narrower than route-weighted sampling intervals for 25 goods, at least 50% narrower for 14 goods, and up to 82% narrower. Conventional intervals exclude the central climate impact estimates of 44% of possible production routes. Route-weighted sampling captures these outcomes and reveals multimodality and impact-category-specific uncertainty profiles that conventional analysis does not. Variance decomposition distinguishes geographical and technological differences between routes from uncertainty within routes, helping prioritize supplier data collection. These differences show that conventional uncertainty estimates can mislead and may not capture how substantially initial estimates could change when supplier-specific data become available.

title: Corporate Green Investment and Debt Financing Costs: The Moderating Role of Green Institutional Investor Attention in China
summary: This study examines the association between corporate green investment and subsequent debt financing cost and the moderating role of prior green institutional investor attention. Using 40,060 firm-year observations from 4633 non-financial Chinese A-share firms over investment years 2011–2024, firm and year fixed-effects models relate investment in year t to financing cost in year t + 1, with attention and pre-investment financing cost measured in year t − 1. Green investment is associated with lower subsequent financing cost, and this association becomes more negative as prior attention increases. At the 25th and 75th percentiles of attention, a one-percentage-point increase in green investment relative to total assets is associated with financing-cost reductions of 2.75 and 3.62 basis points, respectively. The negative interaction persists after ownership and selected liability-composition controls, within positive-investment observations, and under alternative clustered and wild-cluster bootstrap inference. Evidence is stronger for financing-cost measures scaled by total liabilities than for the measure based on average core interest-bearing debt. Period comparisons indicate a stronger negative investment association but weaker attention moderation after 2019, including when 2020 is excluded. Differences across firm characteristics and environmental-exposure groups are less conclusive after multiple-testing adjustment. The findings associate the financing relevance of environmental expenditure with prior specialized investor attention, with the strength of the evidence varying across accounting measures and periods.

title: Unpacking the Governance Innovation Nexus: How Board Characteristics Drive Sustainable Innovation Through Digital Capability in Emerging BRI Economies
summary: ABSTRACT As global sustainability pressures intensify, firms in emerging economies, particularly those operating within Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) countries, face growing expectations to improve environmental responsibility while navigating complex and volatile institutional contexts. In this context, board‐level corporate governance plays a critical role in shaping firms' commitment to responsible innovation and environmental performance. This study examines how board‐level strategic governance influences sustainable innovation among manufacturing firms in BRI economies, with particular attention to the mediating role of digital innovation capacity and the moderating effect of board ability. Using a panel dataset of 496 firms covering 2013–2023, the study applies dynamic panel and instrumental‐variable estimation techniques to address potential endogeneity and strengthen the robustness of the empirical findings. The results indicate that governance mechanisms associated with inclusiveness and accountability, particularly gender‐diverse boards, performance‐based incentives, and board ownership, positively influence sustainable innovation. In contrast, larger boards and longer director tenures are associated with weaker sustainable innovation outcomes. Digital innovation capacity emerges as an important mediating mechanism through which board‐level governance contributes to sustainable innovation. At the same time, board ability directly enhances sustainable innovation and strengthens the effectiveness of governance mechanisms. By focusing on five MENA BRI economies, the study provides context‐specific evidence on governance and sustainability in emerging and transition economies. The findings contribute to the corporate governance, corporate social responsibility, and environmental management literature and offer practical implications for firms and policymakers seeking governance reforms that support innovation‐driven sustainability transitions.

title: Examining governance and sustainability reporting: insights from BRSR disclosures in Indian companies
summary: Purpose The purpose of this study is to analyse the impact and interconnectedness of corporate governance attributes such as board size, gender diversity of board, ESG/Sustainability committee, age of company, profitability, market capitalization and leverage on India's recent sustainability reporting business responsibility and sustainability reporting (BRSR) framework. Design/methodology/approach A total of 101 NSE listed company's BRSR reports for the financial year 2023–2024 were used to prepare the sustainability quality index (SQI). The impact of BRSR framework quality on reporting organisations was investigated using Multiple hierarchical regression analysis. This study used SQI score as the dependent variable and firm age, board size, board gender diversity, board independence, presence of ESG/sustainability committee and presence of women KMP were the independent variables. Market capitalisation, profitability and leverage were taken as control variables. Findings The study's findings revealed that traditional corporate governance attributes like firm age, board size and board independence have no significant positive relationship with sustainable reporting in India. In contrast, the study revealed that modern governance factors, including ESG/sustainable committee, board gender diversity and presence of women KMP, have a strong positive impact on sustainable reporting. Originality/value The originality of this study lies in examining how firm-level and corporate governance attributes influence the quality of BRSR sustainability disclosures among Indian listed companies.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Predictive Analytics in Financial Reporting: Enhancing the Accuracy, Reliability, and Timeliness of Corporate Financial Decisions
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) and predictive analytics are increasingly transforming corporate financial reporting by enabling automated data processing, anomaly detection, financial forecasting, and real-time analysis. This study examines how these technologies can enhance the accuracy, reliability, and timeliness of financial information while strengthening corporate financial decision-making. Drawing on existing literature, the study explores AI applications in accounting information systems, predictive financial modelling, automated auditing, and risk assessment. Previous research indicates that AI-driven forecasting and analytical techniques can improve the identification of financial irregularities, support proactive risk management, and facilitate timely, evidence-based decisions. However, their effectiveness depends on data quality, technological infrastructure, model interpretability, regulatory compliance, and appropriate human oversight. The study highlights the importance of integrating predictive analytics with robust internal controls and transparent AI governance to ensure credible financial reporting. It further identifies the need for empirical research examining the long-term organizational effects of AI adoption across different corporate contexts. The study concludes that responsible AI implementation can strengthen financial reporting quality and support more informed, efficient, and forward-looking corporate financial decisions.

title: CORPORATE GOVERNANCE OF THE PROCESSES OF DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING ENTERPRISE RISK MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES
summary: The article examines the role of corporate governance in the development and implementation of enterprise risk management strategies amid growing uncertainty and increasing financial, operational, market, and security threats. The relevance of integrating risk management into the corporate governance system is substantiated, with particular emphasis on aligning risk management practices with strategic objectives, corporate oversight, internal control mechanisms, and reporting procedures. The study systematizes the principal stages of the risk management process, including risk identification, assessment, prioritization, response planning, monitoring, and review, as well as the main strategies for responding to identified risks. Particular attention is paid to the role of corporate governance bodies in ensuring the timely identification of potential threats, evaluating their possible impact on enterprise performance, and supporting well-grounded management decisions. A structural and logical model of corporate governance in risk management is proposed. The model integrates strategic management, corporate control, and a cyclical risk management process, thereby establishing a coherent framework for coordinating strategic priorities with risk assessment and response activities. It emphasizes the importance of continuous monitoring, feedback, and the adjustment of management measures in response to changes in the internal and external business environment. The practical significance of the proposed model is determined in terms of strengthening enterprise resilience, improving the quality of managerial decision-making, and enhancing the overall effectiveness of enterprise management. The findings highlight that effective corporate governance creates the organizational conditions necessary for systematic risk oversight, greater transparency, accountability, and the timely implementation of appropriate risk response measures. The proposed approach can be applied to improve corporate governance practices and develop more adaptive risk management systems capable of supporting enterprise stability and sustainable development under conditions of uncertainty.

title: Diving deeper: a systematic review of sustainable scuba diving supply chain
summary: Introduction Scuba diving tourism depends on a chain of actors (certification agencies, equipment suppliers, dive operators, intermediaries and divers) that draws on a shared natural asset, the dive site, yet it has rarely been examined from a supply chain perspective. Methods This systematic review, reported according to PRISMA 2020, synthesizes 188 studies published between 2004 and 2026, identified through searches of Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar, citation chaining and a fully documented search of OpenAlex, and selected with a strict supply-chain eligibility rule. Each study was coded for its supply chain tier, design, evidence type and the framework relationships its findings bear on. Results Only 25 studies (13%) analyse scuba diving tourism as a multi-actor chain or system; 148 examine a single actor or process, and 15 adjacent tourism supply chain studies are used for theory transfer. Evidence is concentrated on dive operations, divers and the natural capital foundation, while equipment supply is almost unstudied (eight studies). Observational and stated-preference studies consistently link better reef condition with higher diver demand, prices and willingness to pay, and observational studies associate operator environmental certification with lower reef contact, while the evidence on training standards, supervision and briefings is mixed; stated-preference and modeling studies indicate that moderate user fees can finance management with little loss of demand. Evaluated interventions are rare, the one evaluated quota lost its effect within a few years, and claims about collaboration, leakage, equipment supply and strategic interaction among operators rest on limited, descriptive or adjacent evidence or remain untested. Discussion The review proposes the Sustainable Scuba Diving Tourism Supply Chain (SSDTSC) framework, a five-layer model in which every relationship carries an explicit evidence status, and sets out a research agenda that prioritizes intervention studies, chain-level data on value distribution and the governance of shared dive sites.

title: Calculation of carbon footprint of forestry tourism and optimization of emission reduction strategies in sustainable supply chain management
summary: This study aims to construct a high-precision and dynamic carbon footprint accounting model and provide feasible emission reduction strategy combinations to address specific issues in the forest tourism supply chain, such as blurred boundaries in carbon footprint accounting, static lag in emission factors, and divergent emission reduction strategies in balancing environmental, economic, and social benefits. Firstly, this paper determines the lifecycle accounting boundaries based on the ISO 14067 (International Organization for Standardization) standard, covering upstream material supply, midstream scenic area operation, downstream waste disposal, and tourist return. Then, this paper collects and preprocesses multi-source heterogeneous data, including smart meter data and GPS (Global Positioning System) trajectories, to address data silos and noise issues. Next, this paper introduces a triple dynamic correction mechanism based on load factors, grid time series marginal emission factors, and biodynamic parameters to achieve spatiotemporal dynamic perception of carbon footprint. Also, this paper takes the dynamic accounting results as input and constructs a multi-objective optimization model with clean energy substitution rate as the decision variable. Finally, this paper uses NSGA-II (Non dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II) and elite strategy to solve the Pareto front, achieving closed-loop collaboration between accounting accuracy and multi-dimensional objective trading operations. The experimental results show that the average absolute percentage error of the carbon footprint time series prediction method in this paper is 2.01%; the unit emission reduction cost is 40.97 yuan/ton of carbon dioxide equivalent; the tourist satisfaction index reaches 0.87. The method proposed in this paper combines triple dynamic factor correction with three-dimensional NSGA-II multi-objective optimization, significantly improving the accuracy of carbon footprint calculation in the forestry tourism supply chain, and formulating emission reduction strategies that consider environmental, economic, and social benefits.

title: THE CROSS-BORDER MIGRATION OF CHINA'S DIGITAL GOVERNANCE EXPERIENCE UNDER THE CHINA-ASEAN DIGITAL ECONOMY COOPERATION FRAMEWORK
summary: With the rapid development of digital technology, digital governance has become an important path to modernizing national governance and a key issue in global economic cooperation. Within the framework of China-ASEAN digital economy cooperation, regional cooperation practices centered on the "Digital Silk Road" have provided fertile ground for the cross-border transfer of China's digital governance experience. This paper, from the dialectical perspective of "development empowerment and sovereignty balance," systematically examines the core elements, current status, and pathways of the cross-border transfer of China's digital governance experience. The study finds that China's digital governance model, characterized by state-capacity leadership, infrastructure exports as a precursor, the promotion of technical standards as a link, and multi-party collaborative governance as a mechanism, has generated significant spillover effects in ASEAN's digital transformation process. This cooperation not only provides ASEAN countries with a development path different from the West and innovates the South-South digital cooperation paradigm, but also injects new momentum into the equitable and diversified transformation of the global digital governance system, highlighting the global governance significance of the "Chinese solution."

title: Can integrated legal and administrative governance reduce corporate carbon emissions?
summary: Traditional environmental governance often relies on a single regulatory form, necessitating the exploration of more comprehensive integrated governance models. Utilizing the pilot program of procuratorial public interest litigation in China as a quasi-natural experiment, this study investigates the impact of integrated legal and administrative governance on corporate carbon emissions and the underlying mechanisms. The findings demonstrate that this governance model significantly reduces corporate carbon emissions. Mechanism tests reveal that the policy functions by strengthening institutional constraints, incentivizing green investments, mobilizing public environmental supervision, and heightening corporate litigation risks. Heterogeneity analyses indicate that factors such as executives’ environmental experience, industry pollution attributes, regional rule of law levels, and market competition exert differential effects on the policy’s impact. Additionally, our analysis reveals that the policy further enhances firms’ overall ESG performance. These findings confirm that integrating judicial oversight with administrative supervision is a viable pathway for achieving carbon neutrality, offering valuable insights for constructing a multi-stakeholder environmental governance system.

title: Developing an Integrated Procure-to-Pay and Source-to-Contract Digital Framework for Construction Supply Chain Efficiency in Saudi Arabia
summary: Procurement in construction in Saudi Arabia is a highly fragmented process operating across project organisations, specialist contractors and a wide range of dispersed suppliers. This fragmentation means that there is a significant disconnect between the strategic sourcing decisions and the actual transactions that take place in the delivery and payment of materials, equipment and services. This review proposes an integrated digital framework that links Source-to-Contract (S2C) with Procure-to-Pay (P2P), with construction-specific evidence, contractual authority and supplier involvement being the key design constraints. The framework is the result of a structured integrative review of 30 journal papers from the period 2020 to 2025, which were analysed thematically with respect to e-procurement, construction supply chains, information interoperability, payment governance and digital adoption. The review identifies five recurring integration failures: inconsistent master data, separation of contract and operational records, poor linkage of physical progress, fragmented exception handling and uneven levels of organisational readiness. The proposed framework addresses these through the use of a governed supplier and contract register, project coded requisition controls, evidence linked receipt and valuation, invoice reconciliation and an auditable analytics layer. It clearly distinguishes between deterministic control rules and optional advanced technologies (including model based quantity extraction and distributed verification). Performance is assessed in terms of traceability, procurement lead time, first pass match, payment predictability, supplier access and disruption response rather than on the basis of any assumed cost savings. The contribution is a process to data architecture and a staged implementation methodology which is appropriate for Saudi construction programmes, with the boundaries of the approach being clearly defined by procurement regulations, contract provisions and information quality. As the framework is based on a review of the published literature rather than on a live implementation it provides a set of testable design propositions rather than any unproven operational results.

title: Flexibility Through Integration: Mediated Mechanisms in Pharmacy Supply Chains
summary: This study investigates how supply chain integration (SCI) helps community pharmacies become more flexible (SCF) by looking at the roles of customer responsiveness, demand forecasting, and supplier performance. Using data from 236 community pharmacies in Konya, Türkiye, we tested these relationships using covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM) with a Maximum Likelihood Robust (MLR) estimator and bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) bootstrapping (5,000 resamples). The findings show that integration does not lead to flexibility directly; instead, it works predominantly through indirect steps. Specifically, integration strengthens customer responsiveness and supplier performance, which serve as the primary indirect pathways to supply chain flexibility. Although demand forecasting is enhanced through integration and customer responsiveness, it does not directly predict flexibility; rather, its influence is channelled through supplier performance. The total indirect effect was statistically significant (unstandardised b = 0.952, 95% BCa CI [0.592, 1.468]; standardised β = .559) and the model explained 65.5% of the variance in supply chain flexibility (R² = .655). These results suggest that flexibility in community pharmacies is not an automatic consequence of structural integration; rather, it emerges through the quality of supplier relationships and responsiveness to patient needs. Ultimately, the study provides context-specific insights for improving medicine availability and building more resilient supply chains within Konya's community pharmacy sector.

title: KAP Reputation, Audit Fee, Audit Tenure, and Audit Quality of IDX-Listed Companies
summary: Background: Audit quality forms the foundation of the credibility and transparency of corporate financial statements, yet the recurrence of restatements and of sanctions against public accounting firms (KAP) in Indonesia shows that it remains a persistent issue. Objective: This study examines how KAP reputation, audit fee, and audit tenure relate to the audit quality of firms listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) over 2021–2025. Methods: A quantitative associative design was applied to secondary panel data drawn from audited annual financial statements. Purposive sampling produced 119 listed firms and 595 firm-year observations. The data were examined through binary logistic regression in EViews 12. Results: The binary logistic regression on 595 firm-year observations indicates that KAP reputation significantly lowers the probability of restatement (coefficient −0.9063; p = 0.0268), consistent with higher audit quality, whereas audit fee significantly raises it (coefficient +0.9152; p < 0.001), implying that larger fees accompany a greater likelihood of restatement. Audit tenure is not significant (coefficient −0.1809; p = 0.2025). The McFadden R² of 0.6706 reflects a substantial improvement in fit over the null model, and the Hosmer–Lemeshow test (p = 0.1194) points to adequate goodness of fit. Conclusion: Firms audited by internationally affiliated (Big Ten) KAP show a lower likelihood of restatement, signaling higher audit quality, whereas higher fees accompany a greater likelihood of restatement a direction in line with the economic-bonding perspective while audit tenure does not determine audit quality.

title: AI, Machine Learning, and Cybersecurity for Digital Transformation
summary: Digital transformation has become a fundamental driver of innovation across industries, public institutions, financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, education, and digital commerce. The increasing adoption of cloud computing, the Internet of Things (IoT), big data analytics, mobile applications, and interconnected digital platforms has created significant opportunities for organizational efficiency and service innovation. However, these developments have also expanded the cyberattack surface, increasing exposure to malware, ransomware, identity theft, financial fraud, data breaches, and sophisticated network intrusions. Traditional cybersecurity mechanisms, which frequently depend on predefined rules and known attack signatures, may struggle to identify previously unseen threats and respond to rapidly changing attack patterns. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) offer promising capabilities for strengthening digital security through automated threat detection, behavioral analytics, anomaly identification, fraud prevention, and intelligent incident response. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the relationship between AI, ML, cybersecurity, and digital transformation. It examines major learning paradigms, cybersecurity applications, intelligent threat detection techniques, explainable AI, federated learning, graph-based analytics, and ensemble learning. It also discusses the limitations associated with adversarial manipulation, biased training data, privacy, computational overhead, model drift, regulatory compliance, and the shortage of cybersecurity expertise. A conceptual framework is proposed to integrate data collection, intelligent analytics, risk assessment, automated response, human supervision, and continuous improvement into a unified security architecture. The discussion further considers resource-constrained organizations, sustainable digital transformation, cybersecurity governance, and the economic and societal consequences of cyber incidents. The paper concludes that effective AI-enabled cybersecurity requires a balanced combination of reliable data, robust machine learning models, transparent decision-making, defense-in-depth controls, and accountable governance. Rather than replacing conventional security mechanisms or human experts, AI should complement them within an adaptive, risk-based, and continuously evaluated cybersecurity strategy.

title: Green Credit Policy and Financing Costs in China's New Energy Vehicle Supply Chain
summary: Against the backdrop of China's carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals, green credit has become an important policy instrument for directing financial resources toward low-carbon industries. This study examines financing-cost patterns among 15 Chinese A-share listed firms in the new energy vehicle (NEV) supply chain from 2015 to 2022. Using 115 firm-year observations, the analysis combines descriptive statistics, period comparison, pooled OLS regression, and two-way fixed-effects estimation. The results show that average financing costs are lower in 2019-2022 than in 2015-2018, but the difference is not statistically significant. In the pooled OLS model, firm size is negatively associated with financing cost, whereas the later-period indicators, profitability, and debt-to-equity ratio, are statistically insignificant. After controlling for firm and year fixed effects, the association between firm size and financing cost weakens substantially, and none of the examined firm characteristics remains statistically significant. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for firm heterogeneity and time effects when examining financing-cost patterns in China's NEV supply chain.

title: Herbicide formulations: evolution, environmental risks, and green innovation prospects
summary: Weeds are the most widespread biotic constraint to agricultural production, and herbicide-based control remains the most cost-effective approach in most cropping systems. A herbicide's efficacy, safety and environmental footprint depend as much on formulation as on active ingredient. This review synthesises the global evolution of herbicide formulations, compares regional markets and regulations (European Union, United States, Brazil, Africa, Southeast Asia, China), and analyses the limits of conventional formulations and prospects for greener innovation. Herbicide formulations have evolved through three phases: rudimentary systems (1940s-1960s), environmentally improved systems (1970s-1990s) and functional, smart systems (2000s-present). Conventional formulations achieve only 10-30% delivery efficiency, with > 70% of applied active ingredients lost to drift, runoff and degradation; 512 weed species are now resistant to at least one mode of action. The global herbicide formulation market reached US$38.2 billion in 2023; China is the largest producer (about 70% of global glyphosate capacity) and consumer (US$9.7 billion). No genuinely new herbicidal mode of action has reached the market. Formulation innovation is complementary to, not a substitute for, new-chemistry discovery: improved delivery increases the efficiency and safety of existing active ingredients, but durable weed control also requires new modes of action and integration with biological and agronomic tools. Nanotechnology-enabled targeted delivery, active ingredient-optimised design, bio-based carriers and precision application offer a realistic pathway to more efficient, safer and more sustainable herbicide formulations, and to overcoming China-specific bottlenecks in adjuvants and high-value formulation technology. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: Robust optimal reinsurance and ESG investment under rating-innovation ambiguity and ESG rating uncertainty
summary: ESG ratings are noisy measurements and may also be exposed to systematic credibility concerns. We study an ambiguity-averse insurer that chooses proportional reinsurance and green and brown stock positions while learning a hidden green-quality factor from stock returns and an ESG rating signal. Signal volatility represents ordinary rating uncertainty. A worst-case distortion of the rating innovation represents ambiguity about the observation model, whereas a separate out-of-model drift gtrue is used only in stress tests for systematic rating bias. This distinction prevents robust-control ambiguity from being interpreted as observed greenwashing itself. We derive the reference Kalman-Bucy filter and the separated robust control problem. Shared stock-return shocks produce a mixed wealth-belief derivative and a filtering-hedging demand. Under CARA utility, the value function is exponential-quadratic, stock feedback follows a Riccati-type system, and retention is projected onto q∈[0,1]. The verification result is conditional on explicit admissibility and integrability conditions. Primary numerical experiments with illustrative parameters identify the model mechanisms but do not constitute empirical calibration. Independent numerical checks add Monte Carlo intervals, static and insurance-only benchmarks, original-scale plots, and a 40-design parameter-uncertainty analysis. The learning-strategy intervals overlap substantially, and rating-innovation ambiguity effects are small in CE and warning probability. Tail-risk changes are more directionally consistent across the tested parameter region, but their magnitudes remain small. The numerical evidence therefore supports mechanism existence and conditional downside sensitivity, not universal or quantitatively calibrated economic relevance.

title: The Effect of Internal Integration on Operational Performance with Supply Chain Capability Mediation
summary: The rapid growth of the coffee shop industry in the Special Region of Yogyakarta has increased competition and requires MSMEs to have efficient and adaptive operational performance. This situation calls for integrated internal process management and supply chain capabilities that are responsive. The setting of this inquiry is coffee shop micro, small, and medium enterprises in the Special Region of Yogyakarta, and it investigates the manner in which internal integration shapes operational performance, positioning supply chain capability as an intervening (mediating) variable. An explanatory quantitative design was adopted, executed through a cross-sectional survey. Two hundred respondents were handpicked via purposive sampling, comprising proprietors, supervisors, and staff members who are personally engaged in operational and supply chain undertakings. Information was gleaned by means of a structured questionnaire and then processed with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (SEM-PLS) through the SmartPLS application. The evaluation began with the measurement model, appraised via convergent validity, discriminant validity, and construct reliability, and proceeded to the structural model, which was examined through R-square coefficients and a bootstrapping procedure. According to the empirical findings, internal integration favorably and significantly affects both supply chain capability and operational performance. Supply chain capability, in turn, positively and significantly impacts operational performance and simultaneously functions as a partial mediator connecting internal integration to operational performance. Such outcomes corroborate that fortifying internal integration, buttressed by adaptable supply chain capability, constitutes an indispensable strategy for durably elevating the operational performance of coffee shop MSMEs.

title: IMPACT OF BOARD MONITORING MECHANISMS ON RETURN ON ASSET IN SELECTED CONSUMER GOODS MANUFACTURING FIRMS IN NIGERIA
summary: This study examined the effect of accounting technology expenditure on shareholder’s return in selected consumer goods manufacturing firms in Nigeria between 2006 and 2025. Using an ex-post facto research design, secondary data were analyzed from ten (10) firms listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group over a 20-year period, Panel Regression Analysis was used to examine the extent to which accounting technology expenditure influence return on equity. Fixed Regression also showed that Board Gender Diversity (BOGD) is positive and significant to Return on Asset (β = 0.047967, p = 0.0000). Board IT Competence exerted strong positive and significant effect on ROA (β = 0.126435, p = 0.0000). CEO Duality has positive and significant effect on ROA (β = 0.026689, p = 0.0000). The study concluded that the model specified for the study adequately captured all variables and is of good fit. Accounting technology expenditure is significant to return on equity in selected consumer goods manufacturing firms in Nigeria. It recommends that firms should focus more on human capital investment, as it consistently improves shareholders’ returns. At the same time, management should carefully evaluate R&D and software investments to ensure that they are aligned with long-term profitability objectives rather than short-term financial pressure.

title: Unified Blockchain Provenance and Bayesian Reputation for Additive Manufacturing Supply Chains
summary: In additive manufacturing (AM) supply chains, systems that record provenance and score reputation as separate transactions let lifecycle records and assessments diverge. We present a Hyperledger Fabric chaincode that commits a provenance event, the Bayesian reputation update it implies and their link in one read–write set. An on-chain policy admits ratings only from counterparty organizations; reputation gates authorize future activities but never block recording outcomes. Under client crashes in the measured partial-write window, the unified design produced no divergence in 3900 trials (2900 with version 1.0, 1000 with version 1.1), while a client-orchestrated two-chaincode deployment diverged in all 1000 trials of two control batches. A same-channel InvokeChaincode arrangement also produced none in 1000, at 4.5 ms more endorsement and 11.7% lower throughput at 100 transactions in flight. On four desktops, open-loop load saturates near 12 tx/s, and a 12-hour soak at 6 tx/s committed 98.7% of submissions with no partial record found. Ledger experiments cover gate refusal, failed outcomes, recovery and disputes; with client retry, 540 contended ratings each committed once. A simulation quantifies gate errors and shows that evaluation-time decay reacts slowly when active actors’ performance drops. The scores record submitted outcomes; they are not validated measures of performance.

title: A supply chain life cycle framework using social exchange theory
summary: Purpose The purpose of this research is to develop supply chain life cycle theory using the concepts of supply chain uncertainty, supply chain orientation and social exchange theory. Design/methodology/approach This research employs conceptual research methodology to develop theoretical propositions of the relationships that are fundamental to supply chain processes, while following established theory-building guidelines in supply chain management. Findings Supply chain processes must be examined longitudinally, sequentially and as multiple cycles of events and conditions of multiple firms. Doing so can provide theoretical insights into the birth, continuance and dissolution of supply chains. Originality/value This research offers a temporal, process explanation of how supply chain uncertainty may generate supply chain orientation and supply chain management responses, how those responses subsequently alter uncertainty and how this recursive process may help explain the emergence, continuation, adaptation and dissolution of SCM activities and supply chains.
